text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Suleyman Demirel wrote in a letter to the prime minister that claims by the opposition over police involvement in the underworld were extremely serious and must be investigated.
- The European parliament discussed plans by the Islamist-led government to clamp down on the press.

- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan signed a directive sacking nearly 70 officers and NCOs from the Turkish army for discipline problems in what the media says is a clean out of Islamist officers in the armed forces.
- Turkey's triple Olympic champion weightlifter Naim Suleymanoglu received the World Sports Writers' Association's Eleiko Trophy in Athens.
- Opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says the government wants to cover up a scandal over links between the security forces, the state and organised crime.
- Iraqi oil is to flow again after a partial reprieve in a six-year blockage due to U.N. sanctions for Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait.
- The government is determined to have nuclear energy in Turkey in the face of growing energy demand.
- The directorate of religious affairs issued a fatwa saying men should not have their hairs removed through epilation or have fat removed surgically.

- Islamist Justice Minister Sevket Kazan said he would make 1997 a year for clearing up the hundreds of mystery murders, mostly involving the killings of Kurdish activists, that rights groups say are state-sponsored extrajudicial executions.
